findings.title: Embedded post author link lightness wrongly changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 70% lightness and giving the dark-theme branch 30% instead of 70%. The matching rule in common/base/topic-post.scss (.names span a) correctly uses 30%/70%. Result: in light themes the author name on expanded/embedded posts becomes much lighter than before (visual regression), and in dark themes it renders darker than intended.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness wrongly changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 20% to 50% and using 50% instead of 80% for the dark-theme branch. The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss .topic-map h3) correctly keeps 20%/80%, and the adjacent `.map .number, i` rule in this same file also keeps 20%/80%. Result: the mobile topic map heading is washed out in light themes and too dim in dark themes relative to the rest of the topic map.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length lightness inverted (70% became 30%)
findings.body: In `.custom-message-length`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the two branches were swapped: the light-theme color got 30% and the dark-theme color got 70%. The desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length) correctly uses 70%/30%. Result: on mobile the character-count hint text in the flag modal is much darker than before in light themes and much lighter than intended in dark themes, diverging from desktop.

findings.title: Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing the light-theme appearance (30% -> 50% lightness). The purpose of this PR is to add a dark-theme alternative, not to alter light-theme colors; comparable username styling in common/base/user.scss keeps 30%/70%. The member name in the group members table will now be lighter/less prominent in light themes than before.

findings.title: Mobile group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% lightness instead of preserving it and using 70% for the dark branch (as done for `.username a` in common/base/user.scss). This is an unintended light-theme visual change that also makes the dark-theme value inconsistent with the equivalent username styling.

findings.title: Category badge-notification color missed by the dark-theme conversion
findings.body: This PR converts every `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` color in the touched files to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: (100-X)%))` so colors work on dark themes, and this file was otherwise fully converted (th, td, topic-excerpt, etc.). However `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` at line 115 still reads `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` with no dark-theme branch. On a dark color scheme, scaling the dark $primary lighter by 50% yields a color nearly identical to the background, making the topic/category count badge unreadable — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.
